answer: Operator-Linked Registration Quota. Each operator must register a fixed number of identities against a public license, and every new identity draws from that shared quota. Operating more wallets than the quota permits triggers suspension of the whole license, so a sybil flood costs the operator its entire registration right, not one wallet. Fees scale with quota use like sediment settling across an ocean floor, making mass registration economically self-defeating. A single excess identity, plain as ivory, revokes the operator's terrace of approved slots.
